## The brief

The organisers' request, as the abstract.

::: {.abstract}
- Open the workshop with the morning keynote.
- A tentative title, *Infectious Disease Modelling in the Age of AI*, with
  the exact content left to me as long as it fits the workshop theme.
- One idea. Given my work on composable, probabilistic modelling
  frameworks, bridging renewal-process approaches like EpiNow2 with more
  flexible, ML-friendly components, open with some history of infectious
  disease modelling, a few practical examples from my own experience, and
  use that to lead into an open question on how AI fits into this space
  going forward.
- 20 to 30 minutes.
- The audience is a mix of infectious disease and AI researchers, some with
  little to no modelling background.
- Steven Abrams and Pieter Libin speak straight after, giving an overview of
  different methods, followed by three case studies, so this talk sets the
  stage for that.
:::

## Resources

### Outbreaks

- [BVDOutbreakSize][bvd].
  A live joint model of the 2026 DRC outbreak of Ebola disease caused by
  Bundibugyo virus, built largely with coding agents.
  [Source][bvd-repo].
- [The epiforecasts COVID-19 dashboard][covid].
  Daily $R_t$ estimates and forecasts, 2020 to 2022.
- [EpiNow2][epinow2].
  The real-time $R_t$ tool from the pandemic.

### Agents

- [How I am LLM][howillm].
  What coding agents do and do not do in a research workflow.
- [A workflow for infectious disease modelling][workflow].
  The workflow the agents are asked to follow.

### Composable modelling

- [What we want from an approach][approaches].
  The design considerations, and the two approaches we are taking.
- [EpiAware][epiaware].
  The Julia organisation building it.
- [JuliaCon 2026][juliacon].
  Three talks on composable modelling in Julia, August 2026.
